text:
mira: Heads-up — after last night's adaptive-mb rollout we see a p99 tail increase on streaming-chat across the H100 pool. p50/p95 look fine but p99 jumped from 420ms -> 920ms on chat flows.
sam: ugh. is this correlated with mbsize changes? which config rolled? :thinking:
mira: rolled config:\n```
routing: prefer-streaming
microbatch: adaptive
mb_min: 1
mb_max: 6
pacer: aggressive
kv_prefetch: enabled
```\nIt increased average batch reuse but tail spiked. KV hit rate dropped ~6% for chat requests.
alex: can you paste the flamegraph/span? wondering if kernel choice changed to a fallback path for small-seq tokens.
mira: attaching profiler snippet from last 2 hours (trimmed):\n```
H100-prod-1 stream chat sample:\n- kernel=fused_mha_fast (60%)\n- kernel=fallback_attention (28%)\n- kv_read_wait (avg 6ms, p99 80ms)\n- streamer_pacer_wait (p99 110ms)\n``` 
sam: fallback_attention shows up a lot — that explains tail. when mbsize is small we sometimes hit kernel heuristic that avoids cutlass kernels. what mb distribution are we seeing?
mira: most streaming chats are mb=1 or 2 after pacer. Non-stream completions moved to mb=8-12.
alex: hypothesis: aggressive pacer pushes small batches through without waiting to coalesce, which reduces throughput cost but exposes fallback kernels + KV miss tail. For streaming chat we probably want stricter pacer + prefetch warmup.
infra-bot: deploy:adaptive-mb-v2 started at 2026-03-18T02:14:00Z by ci/canary (job 7893)
sam: quick A/B idea: run canary with pacer=conservative + kv_prefetch=sync_warmup for streaming routes. keep non-streaming unchanged.
mira: ran a quick canary yesterday, results:\n- pacer=conservative, mb target ~2-4:\n  p95 430ms -> 410ms, p99 920ms -> 480ms\n  KV hit rate +4%\n- non-streaming completions throughput dropped 6% if we apply same conservative pacer globally.
alex: that matches tradeoff. So split policy: streaming routes use conservative pacer + kernel_hint=prefer_cutlass; completions use aggressive batching. Also add a runtime backoff: if fallback_attention executes >10% in 1m, force coalesce window + prefetch.
sam: can we add a lightweight profiler metric to detect fallback kernel ratio and emit an alert at 10% so we can auto-adjust? That could prevent regressions.
mira: I'll add a metric: runtime.kernel.fallback_ratio and a smoothing window 1m. Also add kb:runtime.kv.hit_rate per route.
alex: small config snippet proposal:\n```
route_rules:\n  streaming:\n    pacer: conservative\n    mb_target: 3\n    kernel_hint: prefer_cutlass\n    kv_prefetch: sync_warmup\n  completions:\n    pacer: aggressive\n    mb_target: 10\n    kernel_hint: throughput_first\nauto_heal:\n  fallback_ratio_threshold: 0.10\n  action: coalesce_window+=5ms, enable_sync_prefetch
```\nworks for me.
sam: perf regression checklist: add canary, monitor runtime.kernel.fallback_ratio, kv.hit_rate, p99 latency per route, and an automated rollback if p99 > baseline * 1.5 for 10m.
mira: doing canary now with route split + kernel_hint. initial numbers look promising (p99 down to ~460ms in canary). keeping watch for 30m.
alex: also consider a pre-warm pass for clients with heavy long-lived chat (pin kv handles) — reduces kv_read_wait p99.
sam: agree. long-term we should refine kernel selection heuristic to consider recent sequence length histogram and mbsize distribution instead of pure single-request heuristics.
mira: notes/action items:\n- mira: finish canary + monitor 30m (owner: mira)\n- alex: file kernel-heuristic ticket to use seq-hist + mb-dist for selection (owner: alex)\n- sam: add runtime.kernel.fallback_ratio metric + alert (owner: sam)\n- infra-bot: record deploy and canary metrics to perf-dash
alex: thanks — please ping if canary flaps.
mira: will do. :thumbsup:
